_readme: Pages where htmldate's eval_default.json gold is judged wrong, with the reason.
Used ONLY to produce a second scoreboard alongside the original — never to
replace it. Both are always reported. A benchmark author who quietly edits
the answer key has measured nothing.
Rules applied to every entry here:
1. The reason must be checkable from the cached HTML, and the evidence is
quoted below so anyone can disagree.
2. Corrections are scored symmetrically. Where the corrected answer is
null, a tool that reports any date is wrong — pagedate included.
3. Doubt resolves in favour of the original gold. eff.org.2015 was
considered and left alone: its gold comes from a path segment in an
og:image URL, which is weak evidence but not obviously wrong for an
annual report.
Three pages were on an earlier version of this list and have been removed,
because re-reading the HTML showed the gold was right and the miss was ours:

scs78.de

10.06.2018 22:00

is the real date line
ldt.de 08/08/2017 is a real byline
500px.com         <meta property='five_hundred_pixels:uploaded'> is declared
The date also appeared in an image filename or href on those pages, which is
what the first pass found and stopped at.

creativecommons.org.html.reason: The page is Creative Commons' "What we do" and states no date of its own. 2016-05-22 appears only inside data-permalink on an embedded image, pointing at a different post: creativecommons.org/2016/05/22/happybdaybassel/

hertie-school.org.leyen.html.reason: The page is "What's on the cards for von der Leyen?". 2019-12-02 appears only in an href to an unrelated article about health workers in Syria.

stuttgart.de.html.reason: The homepage of the city of Stuttgart. 2017-10-09 appears only in the query string of a "Heute" (today) events link, generated at the moment the page was fetched. It records when the crawler visited, not when anything was published.

austria.info.html.reason: A travel-guide homepage. 2017-09-07 is the default value of a journey-date picker, which renders as the current date when the page is served.

pixabay.com.tos.html.reason: The date is real but is a modification, not a publication: the page labels it "Date of Last Revision". A terms-of-service page has no publication date in the ordinary sense. The single-date gold cannot express the distinction.

gnu.org.gpl.html.reason: The document is GPL v3, whose publication date the page prints in its own body. The gold 2016-11-18 comes from a $Date: keyword under the heading "Updated:" — when the page was last touched, not when the licence was published.
